title: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
summary: Text classification using deep neural networks achieves high accuracy but is computationally expensive, while linear classifiers are fast but often underperform without rich features. The paper proposes fastText, a simple linear model with low-rank embeddings, hierarchical softmax, and bag-of-n-gram features that captures partial word order efficiently. Experiments show fastText matches or exceeds deep learning accuracy on multiple benchmarks (e.g., 92.5% on AG News) while being up to 15,000× faster, training on large datasets in minutes on a standard CPU.

match_target.why: User-specified target: Table 1 AG News test accuracy with fastText h=10 and bigrams; this is the central result demonstrating the method's accuracy on a standard benchmark.

tolerance.why: Rule 2: accuracy-like percentage metric on a standard test set with >2000 examples (AG News has 7600 test examples per Zhang et al. 2015 protocol); paper reports no standard deviation.

requirements.quote: The first weight matrix A is a look-up table over the words.

requirements.stmt: Average word embeddings to form text representation
requirements.quote: The word representations are then averaged into a text representation

requirements.stmt: Linear classifier on top of hidden representation
requirements.quote: which is in turn fed to a linear classifier.

requirements.stmt: Hierarchical softmax based on Huffman coding tree
requirements.quote: we use a hierarchical softmax (Goodman, 2001) based on the Huffman coding tree (Mikolov et al., 2013).
We maintain a fast and memory efficient mapping of the n-grams by using the hashing trick (Weinberger et al., 2009)
